opener_episode.why: It is the closest recent analog to Avery: a luxury seller revealing who really buys six-figure status goods. Avery can do the art-world version ('who actually buys blue-chip art, and how'), drawing on advising celebrities, athletes and HNW buyers. The run of supercar episodes (Steve Hamilton, TheStradman) shows the luxury-asset theme is performing now.

angles.headline: Who actually buys six-figure art (and why)
angles.pitch: The art-world counterpart to the Lamborghini-salesman episode: Avery, who advises celebrities, athletes and HNW buyers, explains who is really writing checks for blue-chip art, with stories like Kris Jenner's $100K+ Hap Tivey purchase at Art Basel Miami Beach 2024.

angles.headline: Is art actually an investment, or a luxury purchase?
angles.pitch: A dealer's candid take on art as an asset versus a status buy, fitting Graham's 'is it worth it' money lens and the show's recent run on luxury-car markets and bubbles.
angles.builds_on: TheStradman 'car market bubble' (2026-08-30) and Steve Hamilton fake-wealth episodes

angles.headline: From street artist to global brand: the money behind Alec Monopoly
angles.pitch: How Avery developed Alec Monopoly into a global brand with sold-out exhibitions from New York to Morocco and major brand partnerships, and launched ArtLife.com (2015) into an eight-figure-a-year business.
angles.builds_on: ICH's rags-to-riches founder and creator-income episodes
